title: Round to f32
starter:
(* OCaml floats are f64. f32 x rounds x to the nearest f32 (ties to even),
   overflowing to inf. add32 adds two f32 values the way your interpreter must. *)
let f32 (x : float) : float = x

let add32 (a : float) (b : float) : float = a +. b
hints: OCaml has no f32 type, but the `Int32` module can convert a float to its 32-bit IEEE bit pattern and back.
`Int32.bits_of_float` rounds to the nearest f32 (ties to even, overflow to inf) on the way to bits; `Int32.float_of_bits` turns those bits back into a float.
`add32` must round the sum, not just the inputs: add in f64, then round once to f32.

answer.code:
let f32 (x : float) : float = Int32.float_of_bits (Int32.bits_of_float x)

let add32 (a : float) (b : float) : float = f32 (a +. b)
answer.explain: `Int32.bits_of_float` performs the f64 to f32 conversion the hardware does, including ties to even, subnormals and overflow to inf, and `Int32.float_of_bits` widens it back exactly. Adding two f32 values in f64 is exact enough that rounding the sum once gives the correctly rounded f32 result.
